campaigns.hypothesis: Every even integer n >= 4 is a sum of two primes.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: State a restricted, checkable lemma (for example an explicit bound on the least Goldbach prime in a named residue class or range) that is not already implied by the 4*10^18 verification or by the ternary Goldbach theorem.
campaigns.next_experiment: The certified mine goldbach_growth lists the 12 record least primes through 20,000; the largest is 173 at n = 7426. Test an explicit upper bound against those 12 pairs. Do not extend the range toward the published 4*10^18 verification.
campaigns.falsification: An even n >= 4 with no prime p <= n/2 such that n - p is prime, confirmed by an independent primality oracle.
campaigns.blocker: Range extension cannot compete with the published 4*10^18 verification; real progress needs a new restricted theorem.

campaigns.method: Modular covering identities with unit-fraction certificates
campaigns.hypothesis: For every integer n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Find a polynomial identity family covering a residue class of primes not covered by the classical Mordell identities, and prove it symbolically.
campaigns.next_experiment: The certified mine straus_identities proves 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z for every positive integer n ≡ 25, 73, or 97 (mod 120), by quadratic identities whose cleared numerator is the zero polynomial. The two classes n ≡ 1 and n ≡ 49 (mod 120) stay open; both are squares modulo 120. The classes Mordell's combinations still leave are n ≡ 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, or 529 (mod 840).
campaigns.falsification: An n together with a proof that no positive-integer triple exists; a finite search failure is not a counterexample.
campaigns.blocker: Classical identities leave quadratic-residue classes uncovered, and known results show identities of the standard polynomial type cannot cover them all; a different idea is needed.

campaigns.method: Exhaustive integer plane maps with inverses certified under Gabber's degree bound
campaigns.hypothesis: Every polynomial map C^2 -> C^2 with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Reproduce the classical low-degree cases (Wang: degree <= 2; Moh: plane degree <= 100) on exhaustive integer classes, then isolate a structured family, such as maps with a prescribed Newton polygon, not covered by known degree bounds.
campaigns.next_experiment: Enlarge the class to degree 4 with coefficients in {-1,0,1} using kernel enumeration per monomial support, and record the distribution of inverse degrees and of tame decompositions.
campaigns.falsification: A plane map with exactly verified constant nonzero Jacobian and an exact proof (an infeasible linear system under Gabber's bound) that no inverse of degree <= deg F exists.
campaigns.blocker: Known results already cover plane maps of degree <= 100, so exhaustive small classes cannot reach new territory; novelty needs structural families.

campaigns.method: Colouring and minor-model certificates over exhaustive graph censuses
campaigns.hypothesis: Every graph with chromatic number t has K_t as a minor.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Choose a restricted class beyond the proved t <= 6 range (for example 7-chromatic graphs with small independence number) and state a checkable lemma absent from the literature.
campaigns.next_experiment: Extend the census engine to 8-9 vertices with a faster canonical labeller, then target contraction-critical 7-chromatic graphs where a K7 minor model must be certified.
campaigns.falsification: A graph with a certified chromatic-number lower bound t and an exhaustive certificate that no K_t minor model exists.
campaigns.blocker: Every graph a naive census reaches is inside the proved t <= 6 range; t = 7 needs much larger graphs and exact chromatic lower-bound certificates.

campaigns.method: Exact homomorphism-density search over certified host censuses
campaigns.hypothesis: For every bipartite graph H and every graph G, t(H,G) >= t(K2,G)^e(H).
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Confirm in current literature that K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle is still the smallest open pattern, then fix a restricted host class (vertex-transitive graphs or small rational step graphons) where the inequality can be proved or exhausted.
campaigns.next_experiment: Extend hosts from unweighted graphs to rational step graphons and run exact local search that minimises t(H,W)/t(K2,W)^15, replaying every candidate with the exact counter.
campaigns.falsification: A host graph or rational step graphon W with exactly computed t(H,W) < t(K2,W)^e(H).
campaigns.blocker: Any counterexample is expected to need large or finely weighted hosts; unweighted hosts on at most 7 vertices give a minimum ratio of about 1.025 for the open pattern.

campaigns.hypothesis: For each explicit pair (n,r), any loopless n-vertex digraph of minimum outdegree at least r contains a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/r).
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Independently audit the public computer-assisted fixed-r=6 proof claim, including proof-to-CNF reductions, finite certificates and cited premises; distinguish restricted result from full CH.
campaigns.next_experiment: Replay the external fixed-r=6 proof corpus on an independent host, verify its published hash and proof traces, and audit the hand-reduction steps before launching duplicate SAT search.
campaigns.falsification: An explicitly checked digraph with min outdegree r and no directed cycle of length <=ceil(n/r).
campaigns.blocker: External fixed-r=6 proof corpus (438 MB) and independent specialist review have not been reproduced in this repo; neither encoding supplies a SAT/UNSAT certificate.

campaigns.method: Finite family enumeration and entropy inequalities
campaigns.hypothesis: Every nontrivial finite union-closed family contains an element in at least half its members.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Verify the exact conjecture for bounded universes before deriving any universal structural reduction.
campaigns.next_experiment: The certified mine frankl_orbits quotients the n <= 4 census by ground-set permutations: 4,958 families become 366 orbits at n = 4, and the minimum abundance is exactly 1/2. The next lemma has to generate canonical representatives without enumerating 2^(2^5).
campaigns.falsification: An exact union-closed family whose maximum element frequency is less than half the family size.
campaigns.blocker: Naive exhaustive enumeration scales as 2^(2^n); structural quotient required.

campaigns.method: Deck-collision search over certified graph censuses
campaigns.hypothesis: Every finite simple graph on at least 3 vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its vertex-deleted deck.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Pick a graph family not yet known to be reconstructible and isolate a lemma that reconstructs a new invariant for it.
campaigns.next_experiment: The certified mine deck_signature separates every graph on 3 to 7 vertices by the multiset of (degree sequence of G-v, triangle count of G-v). Global degree-plus-triangles left 20 excess graphs at 6 vertices; the per-card signature leaves none through 7. A reconstruction lemma still has to pass the computer-verified range beyond this census.
campaigns.falsification: Two non-isomorphic graphs with identical decks, confirmed by independent canonical forms.
campaigns.blocker: Computer verification already reaches at least 11 vertices; novelty has to come from a structural lemma, not from range.

campaigns.method: Exact linear-extension counting over certified poset censuses
campaigns.hypothesis: Every finite poset that is not a chain has an incomparable pair x, y with 1/3 <= Pr[x < y] <= 2/3.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: State and prove a balance bound for a restricted poset class (bounded width or height) that improves on published results.
campaigns.next_experiment: The certified mine poset_balance finds 11 posets on at most 6 elements with best balance exactly 1/3, and every one of them has width 2, which Linial already settled. A new lemma has to treat width at least 3; this census has no tight example there.
campaigns.falsification: A non-chain poset whose every incomparable pair has balance below 1/3, with linear extensions counted exactly by two independent methods.
campaigns.blocker: Published verification already reaches 11 elements; a new structural invariant is needed.

campaigns.method: Exhaustive grid search over GF(p)^n with GL-symmetry reduction
campaigns.hypothesis: Any n bases of an n-dimensional vector space can be arranged in an n x n grid whose rows are the given bases and whose columns are bases.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Specify the next finite case not yet covered here (GF(2)^4) with an orbit-reduced instance count and a per-orbit certificate format.
campaigns.next_experiment: Quotient instances by the stabiliser of the standard basis so that GF(2)^4 becomes exhaustive, storing one grid certificate per orbit.
campaigns.falsification: n bases of GF(p)^n with an exhaustive certificate that no valid grid exists.
campaigns.blocker: GF(2)^4 has about 10^8 raw instances; orbit reduction under the stabiliser is not implemented yet.

campaigns.hypothesis: The exponent of matrix multiplication equals 2.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Replay published small-format decompositions (rank-23 <3,3,3> and recent flip-graph or learned schemes) as exact certificates and record the implied exponent bounds.
campaigns.next_experiment: Add a JSON import path and a flip-graph rank-reduction search over small formats, with every candidate replayed by the exact checker.
campaigns.falsification: Not finitely falsifiable: omega is a limit, and certified decompositions only give upper bounds.
campaigns.blocker: Small-format ranks cannot beat laser-method bounds below 2.372; the probe is certificate infrastructure.

campaigns.hypothesis: A deterministic polynomial-size hitting set can be obtained for a named restricted arithmetic circuit class.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: State field characteristic, circuit shape, degree and oracle model, then prove the exact hitting property.
campaigns.next_experiment: Implement small exact arithmetic circuits and a falsifier that searches for circuits escaping a proposed hitting set.
campaigns.falsification: A nonzero circuit in the declared class vanishing at every proposed hitting-set point.
campaigns.blocker: No restricted circuit class or field is locked down yet.

campaigns.hypothesis: Exact families of d^2 equiangular lines exist beyond individually constructed dimensions.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Replay a published exact fiducial beyond d = 3 with exact arithmetic, and state the precise Galois hypotheses of any proposed uniform family.
campaigns.next_experiment: Extend the cyclotomic engine to the number fields needed for d = 4..8 and replay published exact fiducials there.
campaigns.falsification: An exact failed Gram matrix relation or a missing required vector under the stated algebraic construction.
campaigns.blocker: Exact fiducials beyond d = 3 live in larger number fields than the current Z[zeta_m] engine supports; floating-point SICs are not proofs.

campaigns.method: Exhaustive arc search in projective spaces with frame-fixing symmetry reduction
campaigns.hypothesis: A linear [n,k] MDS code over GF(q) with k <= q has n <= q+1, except n = q+2 when q is even and k is 3 or q-1.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Extend from k = 3 (Segre/Bose) to k = 4 arcs in PG(3,q) for small non-prime q (q = 8, 9), certifying maximum arc sizes.
campaigns.next_experiment: Generalise the arc engine to PG(3,q) with 5-point frames and reproduce known maximum arc sizes for q <= 9.
campaigns.falsification: An explicit n-arc exceeding the bound, verified by exact determinant checks.
campaigns.blocker: The conjecture is proved for prime q (Ball 2012); open non-prime cases need far larger searches than k = 3.

campaigns.method: Algebraic constructions (Sylvester, Paley, Williamson) with exact orthogonality certificates
campaigns.hypothesis: A Hadamard matrix exists for every order divisible by 4.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Close the remaining engine gaps (116, 156, 172, ...) with symmetry-reduced Williamson and Goethals-Seidel constructions, then document the first order no implemented method reaches.
campaigns.next_experiment: Add multiplier-group symmetry reduction to the Williamson meet-in-the-middle search so that n = 29 (order 116) becomes feasible, then implement Goethals-Seidel arrays for orders 156 and 172.
campaigns.falsification: A proof that no Hadamard matrix of some order 4k exists; a finite search failure is not sufficient.
campaigns.blocker: Plain meet-in-the-middle over symmetric circulants is practical up to n = 23 in pure Python; n = 29 needs symmetry reduction, and order 668 remains the smallest open case.

campaigns.hypothesis: The exact value of R(5,5) can be determined by an independently checked construction and exclusion.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Verify a candidate K43 two-coloring or independently certify the nonexistence of a K45 valid coloring.
campaigns.next_experiment: Import and check the published K42 witness; reproduce a small structural exclusion with a trusted proof checker.
campaigns.falsification: A verified K43 coloring would refute any claimed R(5,5)<=43; a valid K45 coloring would refute R(5,5)<=45.
campaigns.blocker: A SAT solver UNSAT output without a verified proof trace does not establish an upper bound.

campaigns.method: Incidence-axiom certificates, Bruck-Ryser sieve and constrained exhaustive search
campaigns.hypothesis: Decide whether a finite projective plane of order 12 exists.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Reproduce a published partial nonexistence result for order 12 (for example a restriction on collineations) before any search.
campaigns.next_experiment: Encode order-12 planes with a prescribed collineation as SAT with DRAT proof output, starting from cases the literature already excludes.
campaigns.falsification: An explicit order-12 incidence structure passing the combinatorial axiom check would settle existence.
campaigns.blocker: Unconstrained search is far out of reach; the order-10 nonexistence proof needed a massive computation.

campaigns.method: Exact rational LP with duality certificates over graphic metrics
campaigns.hypothesis: For every metric TSP instance the optimal tour costs at most 4/3 of the Held-Karp (subtour LP) bound.
campaigns.first_proof_obligation: Reproduce published exact maximum integrality gaps for all small metrics (Benoit-Boyd) with LP-duality certificates, then target a structured class such as graphic metrics of subcubic graphs beyond published ranges.
campaigns.next_experiment: Extend from graphic metrics to 1-2 and vertex-weighted metrics, and enumerate extreme points of the subtour polytope at n = 8 to search for gap-maximising instances.
campaigns.falsification: A metric instance with an exactly certified Held-Karp value and a brute-force optimal tour longer than 4/3 of it.
campaigns.blocker: Exhaustive extreme-point enumeration grows very quickly beyond n = 10; graphic metrics up to 7 vertices reach only a 16/15 gap.

milestones.title: Ramsey R(3,3)=6 reproduced
milestones.scope: Finite toy theorem; not a new bound on R(5,5)
milestones.description: C5 witnesses R(3,3)>5; all 32,768 labeled K6 two-colorings fail to avoid both triangles.

milestones.title: Frankl threshold verified for ground sets of size <=4
milestones.scope: Finite exhaustive test only; not a proof for arbitrary finite ground sets
milestones.description: Enumerates all 2^(2^4)=65,536 families, filters union closure, checks exact frequencies.

milestones.title: Caccetta–Häggkvist verified on all digraphs of size at most five
milestones.scope: Every labeled loopless directed graph on 2–5 vertices (known finite cases only), checked modulo relabeling
milestones.description: Exhaustive n=5 census: 2^20=1,048,576 labeled graphs partition into 9,608 isomorphism orbits (matching Burnside and OEIS A000273); two independent cycle detectors agree. Known result only.

milestones.title: Goldbach partitions certified for every even n <= 200,000
milestones.scope: Finite range only; far inside the published 4*10^18 verification
milestones.description: Least Goldbach prime recorded for all 99,999 even n in [4, 200000], each re-checked by deterministic Miller-Rabin; the deep run extends to 4*10^6 (record least prime 751 at n = 3,807,404).

milestones.title: Erdos-Straus triples certified for every 2 <= n <= 20,000
milestones.scope: Finite range only; known computational verification is far larger
milestones.description: Explicit (x, y, z) with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) for all 19,999 integers, each re-checked by exact integer arithmetic; the deep run covers n <= 10^6.

milestones.title: Hadwiger's conjecture certified on all 208 graphs with at most 6 vertices
milestones.scope: Known case (chromatic number <= 6 theorem); not new
milestones.description: Each graph carries a proper t-colouring and a K_t minor model (t = chromatic number); the census is complete by Burnside counting. Deep run: all 1,252 graphs on <= 7 vertices.

milestones.title: Graph reconstruction verified for every graph on 3-6 vertices
milestones.scope: Known computational range; not new
milestones.description: Burnside-certified census of 4, 11, 34 and 156 graphs; all decks pairwise distinct under an independent canonical form. Deep run adds all 1,044 graphs on 7 vertices.

milestones.title: 1/3-2/3 conjecture verified for every poset with at most 6 elements
milestones.scope: Known computational range; not new
milestones.description: All 1, 2, 5, 16, 63, 318 posets (orbit-counting certified against OEIS A001035); each non-chain poset has an exactly counted pair with balance >= 1/3, minimum exactly 1/3. Deep run: all 2,045 posets on 7 elements.

milestones.title: Rota's basis conjecture verified exhaustively for GF(2)^2, GF(3)^2, GF(5)^2, GF(7)^2 and GF(2)^3
milestones.scope: Known small cases (rank <= 3); not new
milestones.description: Every choice of bases (first fixed by GL-transitivity) has a certified grid; basis counts match |GL(n,p)|/n!. The deep run adds all 1,753,128 instances over GF(3)^3.

milestones.title: Strassen rank-7 <2,2,2> and rank-49 <4,4,4> decompositions checked exactly
milestones.scope: Classical upper bound omega <= log2 7; not new
milestones.description: Sparse exact expansion over Z matches the matrix multiplication tensor coefficient by coefficient; the deep run adds the rank-343 <8,8,8> Kronecker cube.

milestones.title: Exact SIC-POVMs in dimensions 2 and 3
milestones.scope: Classical small dimensions; says nothing about general d
milestones.description: d = 2 tetrahedron overlaps 1/3 exactly; in d = 3 all 108 Weyl-Heisenberg fiducials with entries in {0, +-1, +-w, +-w^2} found in exact Z[w] arithmetic, each Gram matrix recomputed independently.

milestones.title: Maximum arcs (3-dimensional MDS codes) in PG(2,q) for q = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7
milestones.scope: Known (Segre/Bose); not new
milestones.description: Maximum arc sizes 4, 4, 6, 6, 8 with explicit witnesses and exhaustive exclusion of larger arcs; arcs through a frame recount q-2 conics for odd q. Deep run adds q = 8, 9.

milestones.title: Exact Hadamard matrices for 31 of the 32 orders 4k <= 128, including order 92
milestones.scope: Known orders; the remaining engine gap 116 is not an open case
milestones.description: Sylvester, Paley I/II, a Williamson quadruple of symmetric circulants of order 23 (order 92, found by meet-in-the-middle on periodic autocorrelations) and Kronecker products; each matrix checked as H H^T = nI. The deep run certifies 87 of the 100 orders up to 400.

milestones.title: Ramsey lower bounds R(3,4) > 8, R(3,5) > 13, R(4,4) > 17 certified
milestones.scope: Classical lower bounds; not a new bound on R(5,5)
milestones.description: Circulant and Paley colourings checked by exhaustive subset enumeration; the deep run adds Paley(37), certifying R(5,5) > 37 (the best known lower bound is 43).

milestones.title: Projective planes of every prime-power order <= 9 and the Bruck-Ryser table to 50
milestones.scope: Known constructions and exclusions; order 12 remains open
milestones.description: PG(2,q) incidence axioms verified combinatorially; Bruck-Ryser exclusions recomputed by brute-force sums of two squares; deep run to q = 27 and orders <= 200.

milestones.title: Held-Karp integrality gap certified on all 141 graphic metrics with 3-6 vertices
milestones.scope: Known small range; not new
milestones.description: Every instance carries an exact LP-duality certificate checked against all subtour constraints and a brute-force optimal tour; the maximum ratio is 1 for n <= 6. The deep run covers 994 instances up to n = 7, with maximum gap 16/15.

milestones.title: Sidorenko inequality reproduced for proven patterns C4, C6, K_{3,3} and P4 on all hosts with at most 5 vertices
milestones.scope: Known families on a finite host range; the open-pattern data in the same run is exploratory, unreviewed and not a result
milestones.description: Exact homomorphism counts, recounted from the opposite bipartition side, compared by integer arithmetic on all 52 host graphs; P4 attains equality on regular hosts. The run also records K_{5,5} minus C_10 on the same hosts (and on all 1,252 hosts up to 7 vertices at deep level, minimum ratio about 1.0248) purely as falsifier data.

milestones.title: Plane Jacobian conjecture verified on all 59,049 integer maps of degree <= 2 with coefficients in {-1,0,1}
milestones.scope: Known (Wang 1980; Moh 1983); not new
milestones.description: 240 maps have constant nonzero Jacobian (matching brute force); each has an explicit inverse of degree <= 2 checked by composition in both orders, and completeness is re-derived from a separate evaluation-based linear system. The deep run covers all 387,420,489 maps of degree <= 3 (816 with constant Jacobian), every one inverted.

milestones.title: Record least Goldbach primes through 20,000
milestones.scope: Finite table inside the published 4*10^18 verification; not a new bound
milestones.description: Twelve running-maximum least primes, the largest 173 at n = 7426. An independent odd-only sieve recomputes the same record list.

milestones.title: Erdos-Straus residues for primes 1 mod 24 through 8,000
milestones.scope: Explicit solutions in a finite range; not an identity and not a proof
milestones.description: All 117 such primes have a checked solution whose residue 4x-n lies in {3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23}. The equation is rechecked without calling the search.

milestones.title: Union-closed families on at most 4 elements, up to relabelling
milestones.scope: Exhaustive range already checked without symmetry; the orbit count is not a general proof
milestones.description: 4,958 nontrivial union-closed families on 4 elements form 366 orbits. Minimum abundance 1/2. A second canonisation, by sorted subset tuples, reproduces the orbit counts.

milestones.title: Deck-certified degree and triangle separation through 6 vertices
milestones.scope: Census already known to be reconstructible far beyond 6 vertices; this only ranks coarse invariants
milestones.description: Degree sequence separates through 4 vertices. Degree sequence plus triangle count separates through 5 and leaves 20 excess graphs at 6. Both invariants are recomputed from cards.

milestones.title: Posets of balance exactly 1/3 on at most 6 elements are width 2
milestones.scope: Inside the published verification through 11 elements, and inside Linial's width-2 theorem; not a new case
milestones.description: Eleven posets attain best balance 1/3. Their width-height types are 2x2, 2x3, 2x4 and 2x5. Balances are recounted by removing minimal elements.

milestones.title: Quadratic Erdős–Straus identities for three classes modulo 120
milestones.scope: Proved for every positive integer n ≡ 25, 73, or 97 (mod 120). Not a proof of the conjecture, and not the six classes modulo 840 that Mordell's combinations leave open.
milestones.description: For each class, x = (n+r)/4 and y, z = n(n+r)/s, n(n+r)/t with s+t = 4r. The cleared numerator is identically zero as a polynomial of degree at most 5, and the same identity is rechecked at six integer points. Classical in type (Mordell 1967); the explicit expansions are checked here.

milestones.title: Per-card deck signature separates every graph on at most 7 vertices
milestones.scope: Finite census only, inside McKay's published verification through at least 11 vertices. Not a reconstruction theorem.
milestones.description: The sorted list of (degree sequence of G-v, triangles in G-v) takes a different value on every graph with 3 to 7 vertices (4, 11, 34, 156, and 1,044 graphs). Adjacency cards and edge-set cards agree.
